newsitem.title: USA: UPS refuses hotel bills for IPA crews-union.
newsitem.headline: UPS refuses hotel bills for IPA crews-union.

text.p: United Parcel Service retaliated against the Independent Pilots Association for supporting the Teamsters strike by refusing to pay hotel and food bills for nearly 300 stranded flight crews, the IPA alleged Tuesday.
The IPA issued a statement saying the union had decided to pay $150,000 out of its own funds to keep 293 crew members in 54 cities around the country until 1200 EDT (1600 GMT).

"UPS management has overreacted," Capt. Robert Miller, the IPA president, said in a statement. "If they force us to bring our pilots home, it will take twice as long to restart the airline once the Teamsters strike is over."

Over the weekend, the IPA, which represents 2,000 UPS pilots, agreed to honor the Teamsters strike by not crossing picket lines to fly UPS planes. The union alleged hotel privileges for its members were cut off at noon on Monday.

Miller called on UPS air management to rescind the action and keep pilots ready at outbound duty stations. "If the company meets us half way, we will be in a much better position to service our clients when the strike is over," he said in the statement.
UPS officials were not immediately available for comment.
